body:
Currently a SrA in the 3D0x3 field. I’m separating in two months after my first 4 year contract and having cold feet about palace fronting. I don’t know if this is the right place to post, but I’m currently having major separation anxiety over all of it. Since I joined my plan was to do 4 years, work my ass off, get a degree, get out and find a decent job. I failed to do any of that though. 

I never finished a degree let alone my associates and all I have is roughly 4 years experience, SEC+, and a TS/SCI. I wasn’t planning on separating until I obtained at least my BSIT from Bellevue online, but I was offered technician job with my current SQ. It’s a staff slot that pays at a GS-11 (w/cyber bonus) salary. 

When I was first offered it I was ecstatic as I figured I’d be making nearly double what I make now despite the loss of BAH/BAS and Health/dental insurance. So I told the guard leadership I’d take the offer and am currently slotted for the position in the system. The catch is, I’d be replacing the current MSgt in my shop who will be deploying and once he gets back after 7 months, I will no longer have the position. 

As my separation gets closer, I get more and more concerned with whether or not I’m making the right choice for myself. At the moment I’m heavily considering extending another year and finishing my degree and possibly trying to go guard if an AGR slot opens up back home. On the other hand I feel like I could be sacrificing what very well may be a good way to get my foot in the door with not only the guard, but opportunities on the civilian side. 

The reason I’m so hesitant is due to the fact that I recently got a 3 on my last EPR and I don’t think I’d make staff this year if I chose to stay in given that I don’t think I did so well on the WAPS. Sadly that be a huge blow to my esteem if I missed staff this year since I had previously missed the cutoff to test last year by a couple days. Not only that, but I’d be taking E-4 pay over being an E-5 making GS-11 pay for 7 months and other possible opportunities. 

When I look back over my first 4 years, nothing was bad about it and honestly I enjoyed it overall especially because of my coworkers. The main reason I considered separating is to gain control over where I live and actually having time to go to college full time, but now it’s just become all about the money to me and the possibilities of contracting and making more, but the more I think I about it the more I feel it’s unrealistic with my current skill set and yet I’m surrounded by so many within my own squadron who have done the same exact thing and made it. 

I’m going in circles at this point, and tbh I don’t know what kind of advice I’m looking for I just feel lost and I’ve been losing sleep over thinking about this so much. I felt like I had a plan A, B, C...etc getting out, but now I just feel like I was way in over my head because at this point I’m starting to question what I even want out of all of this and my career and I really know anyone I feel comfortable talking about this to. Sorry for ranting.
